issues.text: First time I meet `WriteProblemAsync` and nothing says what it is; I only learn in section 5 that it is a private helper that writes the title/status/detail body. I could guess from the name, so not stuck, but I paused.
issues.fix: At this first mention, add "(the helper that writes the error body, shown below)" after `WriteProblemAsync`.

issues.quote: A `catch` clause never catches an exception thrown from inside itself or its sibling clauses, so it travels outward past this middleware, and the client keeps whatever partial response already went out, cut off.
issues.text: The started-response paragraph is the densest in the lesson; I read it twice. It is followable now (the sibling-clause rule is stated), but this last sentence joins three facts: why it escapes, where it goes, what the client sees.
issues.fix: Split after "past this middleware." and start a new sentence: "The client keeps whatever partial response already went out, cut off."

issues.quote: Without this middleware, a `500` would still come back. But the example app is configured for local development
issues.text: The correction of the first misconception carries a second topic (what ASP.NET Core does without this middleware, Development vs outside it). Each part is understandable, but I had to re-read to see how it ties back to "fails silently".
issues.fix: Start the aside with a linking phrase, e.g. "Even without this middleware the request would not fail silently: a `500` would still come back, but …".

issues.text: Docker/docker compose is not in my vocabulary. Each command's effect is stated right beside it (stop only the database; the API's console log), so I can still run the steps and check the result; noting it only.

issues.quote: never runs when a handler throws

issues.quote: - catch clause order — C# tries a `try` block's `catch` clauses top to bottom
